answer: Wind gates stop sibling keys from sharing one vine. The applicant locks 18.6 POA and receives a 10-byte cipher tag, sealed to a licensed vine on row C-14 from this epoch seed. For 220 minutes a ridge zephyr vane must stay between 204 and 248 degrees while a 7-byte leaf hash is filed every 11 minutes. The registrar recomputes the tag and admits only one cipher per row. Making 2,450 aliases takes 2,450 unshared vines and 49,000 in-window hashes. A reused tag, a vane off by over 8 degrees, or a late hash burns 68% of the lock and idles that row for 16 epochs.
